svg.title: NTP correction with unequal network delays
svg.desc: A starts 10 minutes ahead and B 7 minutes behind an accurate NTP server. Both send requests at real elapsed time zero. A's request takes 30 milliseconds and its reply 10. B's request and reply each take 20 milliseconds. Both clients receive after 40 milliseconds and estimate a 20 millisecond delay each way. After applying their estimated corrections, A remains 10 milliseconds ahead; B has zero error in this idealized example. The server is accurate, replies and corrections are instantaneous, clock rates are steady, and other errors are ignored. Individual one-way delays are known to the diagram's observer, not to the clients.
svg.metadata: Original illustrative diagram. Sources: RFC 5905 section 8, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5905.html#section-8 ; Mills and Venters, Timestamp Capture Principles section 7, https://www.ntp.org/reflib/stamp/ .
